items.bron: British Geological Survey, 'Fossilisation - a visual guide' (earthwise.bgs.ac.uk); Lumen Learning Earth Science, 'Fossils': soft tissue decays first, through bacteria and scavengers in a short time, leaving bones, teeth and shells.

items.bron: BGS 'Fossilisation - a visual guide'; Lumen Learning 'Fossils': the fossil record is heavily skewed toward hard parts, and soft-bodied organisms are scarce in it. 'Veral' correctly leaves room for soft-part impressions, which the lesson goes on to teach.

items.bron: BGS 'Fossilisation - a visual guide': very few of the millions of organisms that die each year become fossils; Lumen Learning: only a tiny percentage of organisms that ever lived became fossils.

items.bron: Hooper Virtual Paleontological Museum, Carleton University, trace fossils 'General Information': body fossils preserve the organism's own parts, as against trace fossils, which record its activity.

items.bron: Paleontological Society, 'Fossil Shark Teeth' (paleosoc.org PDF): sharks shed and replace teeth continually, old teeth drop to the seafloor and are buried, which is why shark teeth are common fossils; enamel-coated teeth resist decay.

items.bron: BGS 'Fossilisation - a visual guide'; Lumen Learning 'Fossils': bones are among the hard parts left after soft tissue decays, and fossil bone is the standard example of a body fossil.

items.blok: Liggaamfossiele is dele van die lyf
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Fossils' and BGS guide: shells are listed with bones and teeth as the hard parts of an animal that are left and fossilise. A seashell is a mollusc's own shell. The sentence gives the beach shell as an example of a shell, and does not say it is a fossil.

items.bewering: Baie stingels is sag, en 'n sagte stingel druk sy lang vorm in die modder in.
items.blok: Liggaamfossiele is dele van die lyf
items.bron: Virtual Petrified Wood Museum, 'Carbonization' and 'Imprints' pages: soft plant parts are commonly preserved as compressions and impressions in fine sediment. 'Baie' is correct: woody stems are also preserved, e.g. as petrified wood.

items.bewering: 'n Blaar laat dikwels 'n fyn afdruk in die klip agter.
items.blok: Liggaamfossiele is dele van die lyf
items.bron: Virtual Petrified Wood Museum 'Imprints'; Saffron Walden Museum, Object of the Month October 2021 (Florissant leaves): leaves are commonly preserved as impression and compression fossils in shale.

items.bewering: Die meeste sade is klein, en tog kan hul vorm in die klip agterbly.
items.blok: Liggaamfossiele is dele van die lyf
items.bron: This is the quantifier 'die meeste', so it is recorded with the superlatives. Seed-mass surveys (e.g. the bioRxiv 2024 study of 2093 western North American species; grassland studies that put common species at about 0.1-2 mg) show that typical species have seeds of a milligram or less, which is small by any everyday measure. Fossil seeds are a standard category of plant body fossil (Virtual Petrified Wood Museum).

items.bewering: 'n Blaar is nie hard soos 'n tand of 'n been nie. Tog kry ons baie fossiele van blare, stingels en sade.
items.bron: Saffron Walden Museum (Florissant leaf fossils); Virtual Petrified Wood Museum 'Carbonization': plant fossils, especially leaves, are abundant where they are buried quickly in fine sediment.

items.bewering: Soms val 'n blaar in sagte modder en druk sy vorm daarin vas. Nog sand en modder hoop bo-op daardie laag op. Die gewig pers die lae saam en druk die water tussen die korrels uit. Oor 'n baie lang tyd word die modder so hard soos klip. Die blaar self vergaan, maar sy vorm kan in die klip agterbly. Ons noem daardie vorm 'n afdruk.
items.bron: Carnegie Museum of Natural History, 'Jurassic Days: make fossil impressions' (the organism lands in mud, leaves an imprint, disappears, the impression remains); Saffron Walden Museum, October 2021 (as the sediments compacted and hardened into shale the imprints became impression fossils); compaction reduces pore volume and drives out water. The steps and their order are correct. 'So hard soos klip' is a fair simile: the mud does become rock (shale or mudstone). Mapping checked: a learner who reasons on from it is not led astray. Where some carbon remains the fossil is a compression rather than a pure impression; 'kan' covers that.

items.bewering: Stap kaalvoet op nat modder en jy laat 'n voetspoor agter. Daardie spoor is nie 'n stuk van jou lyf nie. Diere het lank gelede net so hulle spore in die modder gemaak.
items.bron: Science News Explores, 'Let's learn about trace fossils' (snexplores.org); Hooper Museum, Carleton University: footprints are impressions made in soft sediment by animals walking, and they record activity, not the body. Mapping checked: a footprint in wet mud and a fossil track are made the same way, and neither is part of the body. The comparison does not claim that the learner's print becomes a fossil.

items.bewering: 'n Spoorfossiel is 'n fossiel van 'n teken wat 'n plant of dier agtergelaat het, nie van 'n deel van sy lyf nie.
items.bron: Hooper Museum, Carleton University, trace fossils 'General Information': trace fossils (ichnofossils) are records of biological activity, not the preserved organism itself. Root cavities are listed among them, so including plants is correct.

items.bewering: Vra by elke fossiel of 'n deel van die plant of dier se lyf self daar gelê het en toegegooi is. Is die antwoord ja, dan het jy 'n liggaamfossiel voor jou. Het 'n lewende plant of dier eerder iets gedoen of gemaak, dan is dit 'n spoorfossiel.
items.bron: Hooper Museum, Carleton University: trace fossils form only while the organism is alive and result from its actions, unlike body fossils, which preserve its parts. Tested as a rule against every item in the lesson: a leaf impression, a shark tooth and an egg with an embryo come out as body fossils, and a footprint, a nest, an egg without an embryo and dung come out as trace fossils. This matches the lesson's own classifications and the sources.

items.bewering: Voetspore wys waar 'n dier geloop het en gee 'n goeie idee van hoe groot sy pote was. Sommige voetspore lê nog as fossiele in die klip.
items.bron: Brooklyn College Geology, 'Behavioral adaptation' (academic.brooklyn.cuny.edu); UT Austin Science Museum trackway activity: fossil trackways record where an animal walked, and print length gives the foot size (and is used to estimate hip height). The lesson claims only the foot size, which is the measured quantity, so it is safe.

items.bewering: 'n Nes is 'n plek wat 'n dier bou, en dit kan ook 'n fossiel word.
items.bron: Hooper Museum, Carleton University, 'Eggs and Nests': nests built in or on the substrate are preserved as trace fossils.

items.bewering: 'n Eier wat lank gelede in 'n nes gelê het, kan self 'n fossiel word.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Egg fossil'; Hooper Museum 'Eggs and Nests': fossil eggs are well known, with rigid-shelled eggs the most likely to survive.

items.bewering: Mis is die vaste afval wat 'n dier uitwerp, en dit word ook soms 'n fossiel.
items.bron: Science News Explores, 'Let's learn about trace fossils'; Smithsonian NMNH blog (2023) on ground-sloth dung; Hooper Museum: coprolites are fossilised dung, counted as trace fossils.

items.bewering: 'n Seedier se dop was 'n deel van sy eie lyf en is dus 'n liggaamfossiel.
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Fossils'; Hooper Museum: shells are hard parts of the organism itself, so fossil shells are body fossils.

items.bewering: 'n Dinosourus het haar eiers gelê, en hulle is dus spoorfossiele. Wetenskaplikes tel wel 'n eier met 'n babadier nog binne-in as 'n liggaamfossiel.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Egg fossil': 'As evidence of the physiological processes of an animal, egg fossils are considered a type of trace fossil', and an egg that preserves the remains of the embryo counts as a body fossil as well; Hooper Museum 'Eggs and Nests' lists eggs among trace fossils. One activity sheet (Academy of Natural Sciences, 'Trace Fossil Vs Body Fossil') labels an egg a body fossil. That is a classroom handout against the general convention, so the lesson's reading is the better-supported one and its embryo exception is accurate. Strictly, an embryo makes the egg a body fossil AS WELL as a trace fossil; 'tel ... as 'n liggaamfossiel' does not deny that, so this is not a contradiction.

items.bewering: Mis kom uit 'n dier se lyf, maar dit is nie 'n deel van sy lyf nie. Dit wys wat die dier gedoen het, en daarom is dit 'n spoorfossiel.
items.bron: Science News Explores, 'Let's learn about trace fossils'; Hooper Museum: coprolites are trace fossils, and they record diet and digestion, i.e. the animal's activity.

items.bron: Smithsonian repository paleobotany paper on fossil Araceae (Montrichardia aquatica), whose venation closely matches the living genus; leaf venation network evolution study (PubMed 40481299), which used venation data from extinct (fossil) as well as living plants. Fossil leaves commonly preserve venation. Mapping checked: the comparison is of visible veins, which holds.

items.bron: Smithsonian fossil Araceae paper (resemblance to living genera); Wikipedia 'Ediacaran biota': some Ediacaran organisms do not resemble any living organism. Their relationships are debated, but the lesson claims appearance only, and that is undisputed.

items.bron: General meaning of 'grain' as used in sedimentology (the particles of sand and mud between which the pore water lies, see the compaction sources cited above). Read on its own, the entry is true.

opsomming: All 31 checkable claims are confirmed, including the only point open to dispute: the lesson classes eggs as trace fossils and counts an egg with an embryo inside as a body fossil, and that matches the standard convention, against which only one classroom handout dissents. There are no true superlatives in the lesson ('die meeste sade' was checked as one), and the three comparisons (the barefoot footprint, the garden leaf and 'so hard soos klip') map correctly.
